title: Saracens SC emerge champions; gain promotion to Tier B | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 27 June 2026 05:22
-     - 0

The winning champion team Saracens SC

*Saracens SC’s Anushka Perera scored 80 and contributed in two valuable partnerships

Nayana Fernando and Deshan Fernando carried Saracens SC to victory with a stand of 95

Governor’s Trophy two-day tournament

Saracens SC won the Governor’s Trophy two-day tournament when they beat Old Dharmapalians SC on first innings in the match played at Surrey Cricket Ground, Maggona Wednesday.

The win saw Saracens SC finish on top of the league standings with 3 points and emerge champions. Lankan CC with two points finished in second place and Old Dharmapalians SC third with one.

There was a sigh of relief and joy in the Saracens SC camp as soon as they passed Old Dharmapalians SC’s total of 270-8. Saracens SC eventually finished on 311-8 and it was an all-round contribution that led them to this success.

“This is a huge achievement. Splendid team work. I am very proud of the team, manager, support staff and the committee for their wholehearted support at all times,” said Saracens SC President Nuski Mohamed.

Saracens SC has been languishing in the Governor’s Trophy for the past two years and last year they missed becoming champions when they lost to Kurunegala SC by six runs. However, this time around they were more determined and focused to win it.

Saracens SC also won the Governor’s Trophy 50-over tournament to complete a grand double for the season.

Continuing from their overnight score of 259-7 Old Dharmapalians SC closed their innings following the dismissal of their centurion Viranga Yeshan for 126 (254 balls, 11 fours). Skipper Shanaka Sampath remained unbeaten on 58 (158 balls, 4 fours, 1 six).

Saracens SC began their reply with the worst possible start losing Janaka Sampath for a second ball duck. But Anushka Perera (80 off 131 balls, 11 fours) who was Player of the Final in the Governor’s Trophy 50-over tournament led a recovery in partnerships of 71 with Amitha Dabare (50 off 60 balls, 8 fours, 1 six) and 87 with Kavindu Nimasara (49 off 58 balls, 6 fours, 1 six). Saracens SC then lost two wickets for one run to slide to 212-6. But once again the players rose to the occasion with Nayana Fernando (61 off 85 balls, 4 fours, 3 sixes) and Deshan Fernando (50 off 54 balls, 5 fours) putting together a stand worth 95 for the seventh wicket that more or less sealed the deal for Saracens SC as they sped past the Old Dharmapalians SC total.

– [ST]

title: Sri Lanka scores major sports tourism boost | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 27 June 2026 05:20
-     - 0

From left: Sports and Youth Affairs Minister Sunil Kumara Gamage, Secretary Aruna Bandara and SC Consultants and Asia Pacific Lions Founder Saabir Cader

By Shamseer Jaleel

Marking a significant step in Sri Lanka’s national initiative to establish itself as a leading international sports tourism destination, a special media briefing was held yesterday at the Duncan White Auditorium of the Ministry of Sports in Colombo 07 to announce a historic international rugby festival and series scheduled for August.

The event was attended by the Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Ministry Secretary, the Director General of Sports Development, and Saabir Cader, Founder and Director of the Asia Pacific Lions Rugby (APL).

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports officially announced its full approval, patronage, and support for the week-long international sports festival, which will take place from 22 to 28 August 2026. DASA Group UK, a leading London-based international organisation, has come on board as the main sponsor.

Key Highlights of the Tournament and Sports Festival:

First-ever Sri Lanka tour by an English Premiership Club

Northampton Saints, one of England’s leading Premiership Rugby clubs, alongside the Asia Pacific Lions, will lock horns at the Racecourse Ground. It marks the first visit to Sri Lanka by a club representing the English Premiership. The touring squad will include 10 current England international rugby players.

Australian rugby legend David Campese will serve as Rugby Director for the event, while former Australian captain Will Genia and several other internationally acclaimed rugby stars will also participate.

23 August: T20 charity match

A special charity T20 cricket match will be held featuring international rugby stars against a team of former Sri Lankan cricket legends.

The tour will provide valuable international training opportunities for the Sri Lanka XVs rugby squad. In addition, a special “Coach the Coach” program will be conducted for local rugby coaches, along with community outreach sessions across the island.

28 August: Grand rugby showdown

The tour’s flagship rugby match will take place at the Racecourse International Stadium in Colombo, promising a world-class sporting spectacle.

Through this major international sporting event and investment, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and the Government of Sri Lanka aim to further promote the country globally as a safe, attractive, and world-class sports tourism destination.

title: Skipper Dhananjaya de Silva rescues Sri Lanka with 13th Test ton | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 27 June 2026 04:55
-     - 0

Shamar Joseph struck twice in his first over

Sonal Dinusha sweeps in his 43 out of a partnership of 99 with Dhananjaya de Silva

Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva were involved in a fruitful 68-run stand

First Test against West Indies at Antigua

Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva 

celebrates his 13th Test hundred

ANTIGUA: Sri Lanka were bowled out for 308 on the opening day of the first Test against West Indies in Antigua with the highlight being skipper Dhananjaya de Silva’s 13th Test century. On a day where only 72.5 overs were bowled in total, West Indies’ openers saw off six deliveries without troubling the scorers.

West Indies’ decision to bowl first was vindicated very early in the Test match as Kemar Roach used extra bounce that was on offer to good effect to dismiss Pathum Nissanka in the opening over. Nishan Madushka received an early reprieve and he appeared to be taking full toll of it when he hammered a short and wide delivery from Alzarri Joseph for a six. But the bowler eventually had the last laugh as he trapped him leg before in the same over before bagging the massive wicket of Kamindu Mendis off the very next ball. While he missed his hat-trick, Alzarri had helped West Indies take early control of the Test.

Dinesh Chandimal and de Silva then joined forces to bail Sri Lanka out of trouble with a fruitful 68-run stand that also came at a good pace. While the pacers continued to pose questions often, Chandimal kept the scorecard ticking with regular boundaries. Dhananjaya also got in the groove when he hit Shamar Joseph for a couple of boundaries in the same over. The momentum had turned around completely by the lunch break following the barrage of boundaries. But post resumption, Sri Lanka suffered a big blow when Shamar bowled a top delivery to breach Chandimal’s defence for 54 scored off 67 balls (8 fours). Not only did Shamar remove the half-centurion, he also gave Sri Lanka more reasons to worry when he dismissed Kusal Mendis for a four-ball duck in the same over with the batter edging one to slip.

At 110-5, Sri Lanka were in deep trouble with the home side on the brink of having a go at the lower order. But Dhananjaya found an able partner in Sonal Dinusha. Playing in just his second Test, Dinusha stood tall alongside his skipper to rebuild the innings. Both the batters also scored boundaries at ease on a regular basis to drag the visitors past the 200-run mark as another topsy-turvy session finished on a good note for Sri Lanka.

However, the final session began with a jolt when Roach broke the threatening 99-run partnership by trapping Dinusha leg before for 43 scored off 75 balls (6 fours). West Indies’ joy was short-lived though as another vital partnership added to their frustration. This time, it was Milan Rathnayake who forged a useful stand of 64 with Dhananjaya. The skipper hit a boundary off Jayden Seales to bring up a stunning century and continued to keep the West Indies at bay. A leading edge finally gave West Indies the breakthrough they desired as Dhananjaya departed for 120 scored off 168 balls with 17 fours. A few handy boundaries from the lower order helped Sri Lanka breach the 300-run mark before getting bowled out on a day where the honours were shared.

title: Ecuador stun Germany to progress | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 27 June 2026 04:48
-     - 0

Ecuador’s Gonzalo Plata celebrates a goal against Germany

Australia, Côte d’Ivoire, Netherlands, Japan, Sweden and US advance

History was made by Côte d’Ivoire as they saw off Curaçao to advance from the group stage for the first time, while goals in either half saw Ecuador stun Germany to also advance.

Netherlands finished top of Group F as they eased past Tunisia in Kansas City, while Japan’s 1-1 draw with Sweden means that the Asian heavyweights advance from the group stage for the third consecutive edition. The Swedes also punched a Round of 32 ticket as one of the best third-place finishers.

In the day’s final fixtures, co-hosts USA fell to a late Türkiye goal in a 3-2 thriller while a scoreless draw with Paraguay ensured that Australia finished as Group D runners-up.

Curaçao 0-2 Côte d’Ivoire

Côte d’Ivoire knew that a win over debutants Curaçao would send them into the knockout stage for the first time and it took them just seven minutes to strike in Philadelphia. It was a goal crafted through the persistence of starlet Yan Diomande and swept home by Nicolas Pepe.

The Blue Wave weren’t without chances of their own but a second from Pepe shortly after the hour saw them exit the tournament, leaving the Elephants to celebrate their history-making progression.

Ecuador 2-1 Germany

Even with Germany already safely through to the knockouts, Julian Nagelsmann resisted the temptation to make wholesale changes and they went ahead after just two minutes as Leroy Sane rolled the ball low past the right hand of the diving Hernan Galindez.

That left Ecuador, yet to score at the tournament, with an almighty task. But it was a challenge they rose to. Nilson Angulo got his nation off the mark and restored parity just seven minutes later as he lashed home from the top of the D. Gonzalo Plata’s late, close-range, volley then won it for the South Americans, who advance to the knockouts for just the second time.

Tunisia 1-3 Netherlands

Needing to match Japan’s result in their clash with Sweden in the simultaneous section-closers, the Netherlands raced into a two-goal lead inside the first seven minutes in Kansas City to take control of the group.

An Ellyes Skhiri own goal and a third in two matches from Brian Brobbey had the Dutch in a commanding position, only for Hazem Mastouri to hand Tunisia a lifeline shortly after the restart. Defender Jan Paul van Hecke, though, struck just after the hour to restore the two-goal buffer and ultimately see the Dutch finish top and set up a Round of 32 clash with Morocco.

Japan 1-1 Sweden

Japan were chasing a win and goals to try and overhaul the Netherlands at the section summit when they met a Sweden side also desperate for a positive result in Dallas.

After a tight opening period ended scoreless, Ritsu Doan’s defence-splitter saw Daizen Maeda sweep home nine minutes into the second half, only for Anthony Elanga to strike back for the Swedes six minutes later. The 1-1 draw means that Japan finish second to set up a clash with Brazil in the Round of 32, while Sweden also advance as one of the best third-place teams.

Paraguay 0-0 Australia

Australia knew that a point would ensure they qualified for the knockouts for a second straight World Cup, while a draw would also likely be enough for Paraguay to join them. With neither side taking many first-half risks there was a combined total of two shots – both coming from Australia – at the break.

The second half was a touch more lively, with Nestory Irankunda and Jordan Bos both sending efforts wide for the Socceroos, who end as group runners-up. They’ll now face the Group G runners-up in Dallas on 3 July.

Türkiye 3-2 USA

With the co-hosts safely through to the Round of 32, coach Mauricio Pochettino rotated his starting XI, with two of those changes combining to open the scoring early on, as Auston Trusty swept home a Sebastian Berhalter corner at the back post.

Coming after just two minutes and 13 seconds, that was the USA’s second fastest World Cup goal. Within half an hour the lead would evaporate though, as firstly a move started and finished by Arda Guler drew Türkiye level and then a Baris Alper Yilmaz strike put them ahead just after the half hour.

The man who created America’s first, Berhalter, then lashed home a leveller from the top of the box to restore parity in the second half, but Kaan Ayhan spoiled the co-hosts’ party as he popped up with a 98th-minute winner for Türkiye.

Despite the loss, USA finished as group winners and are now set for a Round of 32 show-down with Bosnia and Herzegovina in San Francisco Bay Area Stadium on 1 July.

title: Royal ends League campaign with 33-17 win over Wesley | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 27 June 2026 04:36
-     - 0

By Shamseer Jaleel

Royal College signed off their Dialog Schools Under-19 Rugby League 2026 campaign with a convincing 33-17 victory over Wesley College in their Cup Segment Super Round encounter played at Havelock Park yesterday. Royal collected their points through five tries and four conversions, while the Double Blues scored three tries and a solitary conversion.

The Reid Avenue outfit held a slender 14-12 advantage at half-time before producing a far more polished second-half display to seal fifth place in the final standings, while Wesley finished sixth.

Royal made the perfect start, opening the scoring in just the third minute when Dinuka Perera crossed for the first try. Kavindu Hewage added the conversion to give Royal an early 7-0 lead. Moments later, Hewage missed a straightforward penalty that could have extended their advantage.

Wesley responded strongly and reduced the deficit through a try by Yoshitha Shakorn before taking the lead for the first time in the match. Flanker Liam Onasiz capped off an impressive attacking movement with a well-worked try, and Ahyan Johar converted to hand the Double Blues a 12-7 advantage.

Royal, however, had the final say in the opening half. On the stroke of half-time, Hewage crossed the whitewash before converting his own try to restore Royal’s lead at 14-12.

After the turnaround, Royal dominated possession and territory, pinning Wesley inside their own half. Their sustained pressure paid dividends when the referee awarded a penalty try, stretching the lead to 21-12.

Wesley fought back bravely after introducing Fawas, Thiranagama and Lye. Fawas immediately made an impact. Displaying blistering pace, he brushed aside several defenders to score in the left corner, narrowing the gap to 21-17 and briefly reviving Wesley’s hopes.

However, Royal finished the contest emphatically with tries from Senuth Karunawansa and skipper Disas Pathirana, who added the final score to put the result beyond doubt and complete a deserved 33-17 victory.

Referee: Raveen Alexander.

Attention now shifts to today’s decisive final round. Unbeaten defending champions Trinity College travel to Colombo for the 10th time this season to face St. Peter’s College at Bambalapitiya, while Isipathana College host the spirited Zahira College at Havelock Park in two matches that will determine the destination of the 2026 Dialog Schools Under-19 Rugby League title, and whether it will remain in the Hill Capital or return to Colombo.

title: Ireland stun world champions India for historic T20 win | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 27 June 2026 04:34
-     - 0

Ireland caused a massive shock as they claimed a first senior international win over world champions India in Friday’s opening T20 international in Belfast.

With key bowlers missing through injury, debutants Jai Moondra and Matthew Hollard starred as the hosts claimed a 34-run victory to snap their winless streak against India in the shorter format at the ninth time of asking and 12 in all formats.

More than 4,000 spectators flocked to Stormont hoping to see India hand a record-breaking debut to batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.

However, after India decided to hold the 15-year-old in reserve and opted to bowl first, new Ireland captain Lorcan Tucker led Ireland’s batting charge, with his half-century helping the hosts post 182-9.

The tourists made a quick start in response as Abhishek Sharma hit 50 off 20 balls, but Ireland refused to panic with Hollard (3-28) and India-born Moondra (2-26) playing a key role in a historic win at sun-splashed Stormont as India were dismissed for 148 with seven balls left.

“I never expected this, to have a debut against India it’s a dream come true and I couldn’t ask for anything better,” Hollard told TNT Sports.

“My family have come out from Johannesburg to support me.

“I’ve been wanting to come over to Ireland since 2019 but then Covid happened and there were a lot of setbacks. My brother came first and said I had to come so I did and Cricket Ireland have been unbelievable with me.”

The sides face each other again at Stormont on Sunday (13:30 BST).

Ireland 182-9 (20 overs): Tucker 50 (36), Delany 49 (32); Rana 3-24
